deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a working derivation. It is the first page of the table of contents ('Inhalt') of Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse', covering Arts. 1–12. The next page notes that the hand is H. Weber's. The marginal footnote says the table of contents comes 'almost entirely from Riemann'. This matches the 'Inhalt' that Weber printed with the dissertation in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke. Modern restatement of each article:

Art. 1 (definition of an analytic function). w = u + iv is a function of z = x + iy if the quotient dw/dz is the same for every direction of the increment dz. Riemann motivates this by noting that it always holds when w is given by an analytic expression in z.

Art. 2 (mapping picture). z and w are represented by points O and Q in two planes A and B. The dependence of w on z is then a mapping of one plane onto the other.

Art. 3 (conformality). If dw/dz does not depend on dz, then dw = f'(z) dz is a rotation-dilation. Original and image are therefore similar in their infinitesimal parts, i.e. the map is conformal wherever f' ≠ 0. That last proviso is my addition; it is implicit in the original.

Art. 4 (Cauchy–Riemann and Laplace). Write dw = (u_x dx + u_y dy) + i(v_x dx + v_y dy). Then dw/dz is independent of dy/dx exactly when u_x = v_y and u_y = -v_x. Differentiating once more, assuming C^2 (my explicit assumption), gives Δu = u_xx + u_yy = v_yx - v_xy = 0, and likewise Δv = 0.

Art. 5. The plane A is replaced, as the locus of O, by a bounded surface T spread over A, i.e. a branched covering (a Riemann surface over a domain). Its branch points ('Windungspunkte') are introduced.

Art. 6. Connectivity of a surface (the order of connection, defined via cross-cuts).

Art. 7 (Gauss–Green divergence theorem in the plane). ∬_T (∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y) dT = -∮_{∂T} (X cos ξ + Y cos η) ds. Here ξ and η are the angles between the inward normal p and the x- and y-axes, which accounts for the minus sign.

Art. 8 (boundary coordinates). Each point of a line gets an arc length s and a normal coordinate p. The signs are coupled by ∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p; consequently ∂y/∂s = -∂x/∂p. This fixes the orientation of the boundary relative to the inner normal.

Art. 9. Apply Art. 7 when X_x + Y_y = 0 throughout. Then the boundary integral of X dy - Y dx vanishes, and the integral is path-independent on simply connected pieces.

Art. 10. Conditions under which a function u that is harmonic (generally speaking) inside a surface T simply covering A is finite and continuous, together with all its derivatives. In effect this is about removable singularities of harmonic functions; it rests on Green's representation formula with the logarithmic kernel. The phrase 'einfach zusammenhängenden' is struck through here.

Art. 11. Properties of such harmonic functions: mean value property, maximum principle, analyticity.

Art. 12. The same question for a complex function w of z on a simply covering, simply connected T. This gives a regularity and removable-singularity criterion for holomorphic functions.

The page continues on the next folio: Dirichlet principle (Arts. 16–18) and Riemann mapping theorem (Art. 21).
errors: No mathematical errors in the stated results.

Art. 7 hypothesis: only continuity of X and Y is stated. The theorem also needs the derivatives ∂X/∂x and ∂Y/∂y to exist and be integrable (implicit in the original); this is a looseness of rigor, not an error.
Art. 4: deriving the Laplace equations tacitly assumes twice-differentiability / equality of mixed partials. Riemann treats this as given here and only justifies it later, in Arts. 10–12.

transcription_corrections: Item 2: 'erscheint[?]' is consistent with the image and with the printed Werke text ('erscheint als eine Abbildung').
Item 8: the uncertain first word '[Festsetzung?]' should be checked against the Werke; the printed dissertation contents may read 'Bestimmung'. Unsure.
Item 10: the struck-through words appear to be 'einfach zusammenhängenden', so 'einfach bedeckenden' alone remains; the transcription is correct.
Marginal footnote: reads approximately '¹) diese Inhaltsübersicht rührt fast vollständig von Riemann her.' The folio number 105 is in the right margin.
